note: Road passages of the hubs layer (forge nav layers hubs, rust/crates/forge-nav/src/hubs.rs; compiled in): a hostile post the only road between two parts of a continent runs through. Every hub of `side` on map `map` whose disks `road` crosses is written with "passage": true: it stays listed (a walk through it still reads "Hostile town"), and its disks price no walk (the walking maps' hub bits, the walk graphs' ground), so a walk keeps to the road through it instead of a way round many times as long.
`road` is the road through the post: world yards in the client's UnitPosition frame (x north, y west), from one side of it to the other, kept off the posts beside the road it does not run through.

Add one only for the only road through a hostile post: the sweep of guide walks near hostile hubs (each walk with its side's price and with none) shows walks many times their hub-free length that all go round it, and there is no other way through. A post with a way round, however long the walk round it, is no passage.

passages.name: The Dun Algaz pass (Wetlands to Loch Modan)
passages.why: The only road between the Eastern Kingdoms' north (the Wetlands, Arathi, Hillsbrad) and its south (Loch Modan, the Badlands, the Burning Steppes) runs through the Alliance posts at Dun Algaz. Priced as hostile ground, Horde walks between them went round the coast past Stormwind: Thandol Span to the Valley of Fangs 19,014 yd against about 5,700 on the road, and six more guide walks 7,000 to 13,000 yd longer.
